transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As we prepare to move forward on the $40 million commercial paper issuance with a 90-day maturity for the seasonal inventory funding, I need to run through our standard pre-launch checks before I authorize the issue. I'd like to hear from each of you on your respective areas. Liquidity risk — please report any constraints or execution requirements you see. Investor coverage — let me know if there are any issues on your end. And legal — please flag any documentation or regulatory requirements we need to address. Once I've collected your input, I'll finalize the terms and record any newly reported constraints or confirmed requirements that affect the final terms, along with the execution commitments for the affected desks. Who'd like to go first?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Elena, I need to flag a constraint from this morning's liquidity stress review. Our internal policy caps commercial paper maturing within 90 days at exactly $25,000,000. The proposed $40,000,000 issuance at 90-day maturity would exceed this limit by $15,000,000. I should note that this updated limit has not yet been entered in the issuance dashboard, so it may not be visible there yet, but it is effective. This constraint affects the final terms of the issuance — either the principal amount needs to be reduced to $25,000,000 or the maturity extended beyond 90 days to remain within policy.

transcript.text: Elena, on the legal side, I need to flag a requirement that affects the final terms. In the current securities-law opinion issued this week, the notes may be issued only to qualified institutional buyers and must carry a qualified-institutional-buyer legend. This requirement has not yet been added to the term sheet. The term sheet will need to be updated to include the QIB legend before launch, and the affected desk will need an execution commitment to ensure placement is limited to qualified institutional buyers.
